clue.text: Drink problem on team displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sports team is showing signs of a drinking problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus-flavoured hot or iced beverage is a kind of drink, so the general word covers this example.

clue.text: Poetry spoken by popular deity

indicators.note: spoken says the word for poetry is to be taken by how it is said, not how it is written

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, so poetry gives ODE
in means fashionable or popular, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Verse recited aloud by a well-liked god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' turns ODE into its sound-alike OD, which then takes IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology is a deity, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: A top circle mountain butterfly

parts.note: to poll a tree is to cut off its top, so top gives POLL
O is the circle shape of the letter

explanation.surface: A sequence of words with no clear scene: a summit circled, then a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo is a large white butterfly of alpine regions, so it is a mountain species by name.

clue.text: Crafty manoeuvre which a clipper might perform?

definitions.meaning: a manoeuvre by a craft, a boat bringing itself alongside a quay
a clipper (shears) cuts short an animal's tail, the trimming of tails

explanation.surface: A clipper ship performing a cunning manoeuvre at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' means of a craft, not cunning; the clipper is a pair of shears, not the sailing ship it suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats berth at a quay, and farmers cut lambs' tails short; both acts share one word.

clue.text: Prime murder victim's name left off

indicators.note: off says the letter for left is taken away from the word for name

parts.note: a label is a name tag, so name gives LABEL

explanation.surface: The name of the first murder victim has been omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain killed his brother, the first murder in the Bible, making that brother the first victim.

clue.text: Revolutionary lancer's aid made flesh

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cavalryman's helper in the revolution has been incarnated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges the letters of LANCERS AID.
explanation.definitionFit: To render something bodily or fleshly is a near-synonym of incarnate, given human flesh.

clue.text: Number turned against terrorist group's spiritual knowledge

indicators.note: turned says the word for number is read backwards

parts.note: a song is a musical number
IS is short for Islamic State

explanation.surface: A figure turned against a terrorist group's mystical insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SONG to GNOS; 'Number' is a musical piece, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for knowing came to mean esoteric insight into divine matters, prized by Gnostics.

clue.text: Metal cast put round to pave the way

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown into a new shape

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Molten metal is cast and set around something to prepare a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like metalworking but rearranges PUT into UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare for or precede an event is to clear its path; the phrasal verb is a near-synonym idiom.

clue.text: See 15
Loaf's a short time in progress

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
something on is happening, in progress

explanation.surface: A loaf of bread spends only a short while in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' is a verb, to idle about, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift around aimlessly or dreamily is to idle, which is what loafing means as a verb.

clue.text: Dig rows? Small probability

parts.note: dig is slang for like, as in 'I dig that music'
rows are lines
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Digging rows in a garden, with little chance of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' is slang for enjoy, not spadework.
explanation.definitionFit: How probable something is equals its chance of happening; the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Austere oast houses shown in 3-D

indicators.note: houses says the clue words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Plain buildings for drying hops displayed in three dimensions; an oast house is a kiln for drying hops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like part of 'oast houses' but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for stereoscopic, giving an image the illusion of depth in three dimensions.

clue.text: Soldiers onto drama (oil spillage) that prompts an early uprising?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: spillage suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops are sent onto a dramatic oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spillage' rearranges DRAMA and OIL into DIOALARM; 'uprising' is getting up, not a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside clock that plays a station to wake the sleeper is what gets someone up early.

clue.text: Expendable Bugs Society

parts.note: to bug someone is to needle or irritate them

explanation.surface: An insect society that nobody would miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' is a verb, annoys, not insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnecessary can be spared; being dispensable is near-synonymous with being expendable.

clue.text: Adolf's companion volume, carried by each supporter, in need of substantial organisation

indicators.note: carried by says the volume letter sits inside the abbreviation for each

parts.note: V is the symbol for volume
a bra is a supporting undergarment
the UN, the United Nations, is a large organisation

explanation.surface: A book carried by every fan of a big organisation, Hitler's associate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' is underwear, not a fan; 'in need of' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler's long-time partner, whom he married the day before their deaths, was his companion.

clue.text: Arrival that's between flights

definitions.meaning: an aircraft's touchdown is its arrival
the level platform between two flights of stairs

explanation.surface: An arrival at an airport during a stopover between flights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flights' suggests aircraft, but the second sense is flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching down marks a plane's arrival, and a stair platform lies between two staircases.

clue.text: Charlie's unit of luminance

definitions.meaning: a charlie is British slang for a fool or idiot
a unit equal to one candela per square metre

explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a fool, as a charlie is; and the name is also given to a measure of brightness.

clue.text: Container clue (cryptic) involves "reversing resort"

indicators.note: involves says one piece wraps around the other
cryptic suggests the word clue is disguised, its letters rearranged
reversing says the word for resort is read backwards

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue that holds a quoted phrase about reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'clue' is fodder, not a description, and 'cryptic' in brackets is the anagram signal; 'involves' puts CULE around APS.
explanation.definitionFit: A small case or pod that holds something, like a time or space version, is a container.

clue.text: Where to get a drink with vermouth, overlooking yard setting

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue means the earlier pieces sit above the next

parts.note: the local is one's neighbourhood pub
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A pub drink with vermouth, served in a spot looking out over a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, gin and It is gin with Italian (sweet) vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A place or neighbourhood where something happens is its setting; the two nouns are near-synonyms.

clue.text: See about wrapping box and put in shade

indicators.note: wrapping says the rearranged letters go around the other piece
about suggests the letters of see are turned around into a new order

parts.note: to box someone's ears is to clip them, a light blow

explanation.surface: Look around while wrapping a box and leave it in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters, split as E and SE to go around; 'box' is a cuff round the ear, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine or overshadow someone, or block a body's light, casts them into obscurity.

clue.text: Fancy acting so sceptical

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Such showy acting leaves an audience doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: One who doubts that God's existence can be known is doubtful, a sceptic about religion.

clue.text: For instance, getting up skirt is one sign

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue says the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: eg abbreviates for example, for instance
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Getting up a skirt, for instance, is a sign of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins constellation gives its name to one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Script's opening extract: "Get into bed"

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word script

parts.note: to educe is to draw out or extract

explanation.surface: An opening extract from a film script, with the line 'Get into bed'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract' looks like a noun, a passage, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone into sex is to tempt them to bed, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: A major wanderer rested by vessel

parts.note: sat means rested on a seat
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A senior army officer on his travels has rested beside a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: Planet comes from the Greek for wanderer; 'A major' is one of the large planets, not an army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets were called wanderers by the Greeks, and this gas giant is one of the major ones.

clue.text: Where to shop wearing belt? It might well contain a catch

definitions.text: It might well contain a catch

indicators.note: wearing says one piece is dressed in the other, the belt going round

parts.note: to belt along is to sprint
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Shopping somewhere while wearing a belt that may have a hidden fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' is a verb, run fast, not a strap; 'catch' is a hidden snag, not a buckle.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine-type terms in a contract are where an unwelcome condition or snag is often concealed.

clue.text: See 26
One of life's professions that is covered by a postman?

definitions.meaning: a ... of life is an occupation or profession

definitions.text: that is covered by a postman?
definitions.meaning: a postman's round, the route covered on foot delivering mail

explanation.surface: Delivering mail is one profession that a postman takes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' means travelled along, not insured or concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'walk of life' names a calling, and a mail round on foot is a carrier's route.

clue.text: Part of this clue shows promise and flexibility

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
play is give or freedom of movement, as in play in a rope

explanation.surface: A clue that boasts of showing promise and flexibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at itself: the part that builds the answer is the subsidiary indication.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cryptic clue has a definition plus a building instruction; the instruction is this part.

clue.text: Roman emperor is not quite a Roman emperor before the state

indicators.note: before says the shortened name comes ahead of the state
not quite says the last letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Nero was the notorious Roman emperor
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor falls just short of another emperor, ranking below the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of NERO to give NER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerva ruled Rome briefly from 96 to 98 AD, the first of the so-called Five Good Emperors.

clue.text: Conversely, one's in story about female society

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the other piece
about suggests the letters of story are moved around

parts.note: or can introduce the converse alternative, so conversely gives OR
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Taking the opposite view, one appears in a story about a women's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the fodder to SORTY, split as SOR and TY around ORI; 'Conversely' stands for 'or', as in 'or the other way round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American college club for women students is a sisterhood, a female society.
